answer: An agent network can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote on reputation or claim scarce tasks. The protocol caps each bond’s influence and slashes it when a challenge proves coordinated deception, using independent task evidence rather than an echo of other agents’ claims. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital in every fake account and risk losing it; scaling a harbor of identities becomes costly, not merely a matter of writing each one a sonnet.
